transcript:
Header: 2026-10-07 15:00 UTC, Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (BrightCart - Head of ML), Ethan Chen (BrightCart - Platform Eng), Sophie Kim (BrightCart - CTO)

Summary: Quick migration demo focused on API parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood, review of streaming and function-calling parity, discussion of hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), and next steps for benchmarks and pricing.

Topics: API mapping, streaming & function calling, embeddings parity, console walkthrough (Optimize suggestions), batching/latency tradeoffs, security (SOC2, KMS), rollout plan.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood. Priya and I will walk through how to map your current OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls to Redwood API, show the console, and discuss perf/cost.
00:18 Maya: Thanks. High level — we're evaluating switching our inference from OpenAI to a provider where we can control costs and get dedicated capacity for high throughput cart personalization. We want parity — api surface, streaming, and function calls.
00:36 Priya: Great. We'll start with a quick parity map. On OpenAI you probably call /v1/chat/completions with model gpt-4o or gpt-4 and pass messages, temperature, max_tokens, and sometimes function_call. On Redwood the endpoint is /v1/generate (or /v1/chat for chat-style), same fields but slight parameter names. Example: temperature, max_tokens are identical, streaming uses chunked SSE.
01:02 Ethan: Will our function-calling payloads work the same? We heavily rely on structured function responses.
01:09 Priya: Yes — we support function/tool calling. There are small schema differences: Redwood's function_call has "call": {"name": "...", "arguments": {...}} in the streamed chunks versus OpenAI's incremental 'function_call' fragments — we'll include an example in the spreadsheet. Streaming behavior mirrors what you're used to but note our event types can include route metadata when using Dedicated.
01:35 Sophie: What about Anthropic/Together? Our NLU team tested Claude-style assistants.
01:40 Priya: For Anthropic, mapping is similar but prompt formatting changes (system vs assistant tokenization and stop sequences). Together models often expose a simple completion API; we map those to Redwood chat or generate primitives and provide a small shim in the examples repo.
01:58 Jordan: I'll call out the common gaps we see: 1) function-calling incremental fragments — we handle them slightly differently but provide client libs with helpers; 2) streaming token prefixes and metadata can vary; 3) model names change. We maintain a model catalog that lists recommended equivalent models with expected latency and token costs.
02:22 Maya: Can you show the console? Specifically how Optimize recommends batching/quantization?
02:28 Priya: Sure — opening Redwood Console. (screen share noise) In Console -> Optimize we show workload analysis: sequence length distribution, token heatmap, and suggested quantization level per model. For your cart personalization, our suggestion is a 4-bit quantized Llama variant for Dedicated if you need throughput or a hosted non-quantized model for best quality.
03:05 Ethan: Any impact on latency when using quantized models?
03:08 Priya: Slightly higher CPU/GPU kernel overhead early but significant memory improvements enabling larger batch sizes; end-to-end p50 latency might be similar or better with batching. We'll show numbers in the benchmark.
03:22 Jordan: On routing: Redwood can route by policy — you can prefer low-latency in us-east for checkout flows and cheaper background batches in other regions. That helps cost without sacrificing critical latency.
03:40 Maya: Security: we need SOC2, SSO, audit logs, KMS integration. Does Redwood provide that?
03:46 Jordan: Yes — SOC2, SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC, audit logs, and KMS support for Private deployments. For Hosted we offer encryption at rest and in transit and customer-managed keys on Dedicated/Private. We'll send the security pack.
04:02 Sophie: What about data residency and on-prem? We're EU sensitive and have some on-prem requirements.
04:08 Jordan: Private deployment (VPC or on-prem appliance) supports EU residency or air-gapped setups. There are enterprise licensing terms for Private; we'll include that in the proposal.
04:22 Ethan: Cost modeling — how do we translate token costs from OpenAI? We need a simple example.
04:28 Priya: In the parity sheet we'll include per-token cost equivalence and show how batching and caching reduce effective cost. Example: if OpenAI charge X per 1K tokens, Redwood hosted pricing is Y but with caching you might reduce effective tokens by ~15-40% depending on prefix reuse. Dedicated has committed rates.
04:52 Maya: Can you run through a live example request mapping?
04:56 Priya: Sure — here's a sample OpenAI chat call: POST /v1/chat/completions body messages:[{role:system...}, {role:user...}], functions:[...], function_call:"auto". In Redwood: POST /v1/chat with messages same shape, functions mapped, add "tooling" pref if you want function routing. Here's the response stream (plays contiguous SSE) — note the function call aggregated at the end for the default chunking but we offer incremental function fragments too.
06:15 Ethan: Are there SDKs? Node/Python? We want minimal code changes.
06:19 Jordan: Yes — Node, Python, and Java SDKs mimic OpenAI semantics. We also have a migration helper library with small adapters for Anthropic/Together prompts. We'll include npm/pip examples.
06:35 Maya: Concurrency — we'll have spikes during peak sales. Can Redwood handle burst capacity?
06:40 Jordan: Dedicated pools can burst within policy limits; autoscaling configurable. We also offer a fallback policy so if Dedicated saturates we can route to hosted or a cheaper model variant to preserve uptime.
06:58 Priya: Quick note on KV cache / prefix cache — Redwood's runtime exposes prefix caching for repeated prompts and can significantly lower token counts and latency for repeated contexts like cart histories. That could be useful for your personalization use case.
07:22 Sophie: Any known limitations migrating from Together models on slot usage or specific tokenization differences?
07:28 Priya: Tokenization differs slightly; Together often has different tokenizer quirks. We recommend running the sample prompt set through the migration script to get token delta. We'll capture that in the parity spreadsheet.
07:45 Maya: Show us the Optimize 'suggested quantizations' UI again?
07:48 Priya: (narration) The UI shows a recommendation: for your median seq len ~512, choose q4_0 on model A for Dedicated, or use model B on hosted for best p95 latency. There's a slider to trade accuracy vs cost and a simulated cost estimate.
08:20 Ethan: For benchmark, can we run a head-to-head with our existing OpenAI/Anthropic fleet and Redwood Dedicated? We need latency, p50/p95, and token-cost per 1M tokens.
08:28 Jordan: Absolutely. We'll run a controlled benchmark if you provide sample prompts and target concurrency. Our usual process: BrightCart provides sample prompt set and QPS profile, Redwood runs a 2-hour benchmark on Dedicated + hosted baseline and returns p50/p95/cost.
08:52 Maya: SLA concerns — what uptime can we expect on Dedicated?
08:56 Jordan: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime (we'll include SLO numbers in the contract). Hosted has best-effort multi-zone redundancy. Private is subject to customer infra.
09:08 Sophie: Legal/procurement question — do you do SOC2 reports and can we get a white-glove security review?
09:13 Jordan: Yes, security team will engage. We'll share SOC2 report and we can schedule a security deep-dive with our compliance specialists.
09:24 (brief cross talk)
09:35 Priya: Demo wrap-up: the parity mapping spreadsheet has three tabs: chat/generation parity, embeddings parity (OpenAI embeddings -> Redwood embeddings mapping), and function/schema mapping. We'll share client adapter code.
09:54 Maya: Do you support embeddings parity? We currently use OpenAI embeddings for search and rerank.
09:59 Priya: Yes — Redwood embeddings API mirrors OpenAI's shape: POST /v1/embeddings with model and input and returns array of vectors. Differences are in vector dims and recommended model names; we'll list nearest equivalents and recommended retraining thresholds.
10:18 Ethan: Anything else on observability? We need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency.
10:23 Jordan: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and trace links. You can create alerts on regressions tied to prompt sets.
10:35 Maya: Okay, recap and next steps please.
10:38 Jordan: Recap — we'll send the parity mapping spreadsheet and sample code by 2026-10-09, Redwood to run initial internal benchmark and then a joint benchmark once BrightCart provides prompt set. Security pack and SOC2 will be shared. We'll propose the 2026-10-15 benchmark slot.
10:55 Sophie: Sounds good. Thanks, team.
11:00 Meeting ends.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription glitches, e.g., "q4_0" might be transcribed as "Q forty" in raw export; product names sometimes spelled differently; timestamps approximate.
